recipes.name: Sweet Potato Burritos
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Heat oil in a medium skillet. Cook and stir onion and garlic in hot oil until onion is soft. Mash beans into onion mixture. Gradually stir in water; heat until warm, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in soy sauce, chili powder, mustard, cumin, and cayenne pepper.
Divide bean mixture and mashed sweet potatoes evenly between warm tortillas; top with cheese. Fold tortillas, burrito-style, around fillings and place on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until warmed through, about 12 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potato Burritos
raw_recipe.description: This sweet potato burrito recipe is made with kidney beans and Cheddar cheese and flavored with tantalizing spices for a hearty vegetarian breakfast.

review.reviewBody: I debated trying these for a long time before I finally did it. I was almost positive they were going to be too weird for us! I give this a 4 instead of a 5 because I made half with black beans and half with kidney beans and the black beans were much better! Also, mashing the beans after they're in the skillet is a real pain. Next time I'll mash them first. I was worried that it was going to be too much cumin and chili powder, but used all the spices just as the recipe suggested and it was the perfect contrast against the subtle sweetness of the potatoes. Next time I'll use a little more cheese in each burrito. Served with sour cream.

We loved these & thought they were far from bland. I didn't exactly follow the recipe though. Some spices, particularly curry, cumin & chile powder, need to be sauteed a bit to help release their flavors. So I sauteed my onion for a few minutes, added the garlic (didn't want to cook it too long as it turns bitter), then a couple of minutes later, added the cumin, chile & cayenne....allowing them to heat for a minute or two. Thsi really pulls the flavor out & makes a big difference. I used black beans (rinsed & drained & only mashed enough to beak up the beans) instead of kidney beans & I used vegetable broth instead of water, only adding enough to make it the consistency that I wanted. I used a mexican blend cheese, dark brown spicy mustard & just mixed my mashed sweet potatoes into the bean mixture instead of loading them separately into the burritos. Once assembled, I gave the burritos a light spray w/ olive oil cooking spray, just enough to fake them out & make them think they had been fried. ;o) Served them w/ fresh mango slices & avocado slizes, sprinkled w/ lime & salt. Brigadiero's (from this site) for dessert. I froze the leftovers on a cookie sheet. I'll wrap them separately in plastic wrap & then put them in a freezer bag. Thansk for a wonderful recipe Karena!

Like others I cut the recipe in half. I only needed about 1/2 Cup water. After sauteeing onions and garlic, I added drained and rinsed kidney beans (2, 15.5 oz. cans) , seasonings and about 1/2 C. water and brought to a gentle simmer. I mashed about half of the beans with the back of a large spoon as the mixture cooked. Simmered until desired consistency for spreading on tortillas was reached. Since only serving 2, I just used the microwave for warming tortillas and burritos, as needed. Delicious flavor combination with the mashed yams . Yummy leftovers too!

I enjoyed this unique burrito and my 3 and 6 year olds ate one as well. I used 1 teaspoon of chili powder and 1 teaspoon of cumin (because of my young kids) and only 1 cup of water. I can't imagine adding 2 - it would be like a soup. At tip - if you wait until the bean mixture has thoroughly cooled, it's much less watery and easier to fill into the tortillas. We ate some and froze the rest.

This is wonderful! Thanks for a great recipe! 

OI used only 2 tablespoons of soy sauce. I made it super easy by using 2 cans of refried black beans and 2 of whole black beans. Didn't have to mash anything. Used no water and can't imagine why it would be used. Didn't even use the water from the beans. Also, cooking sweet potatoes is very simple when you cut them into one inch slices and cook them for 30 minutes or less at 400 degrees. I lightly coat the slices with olive oil and a little sea salt. The skins slide right off after baking. used 2 fat pinches of the cayenne pepper too, and cooked the bean mixture just a couple of minutes after adding the spices. I used Dijon mustard!

The way I like to finish these is by putting extra cheese on top of the burritos and covering lightly with foil, then heating for 25 minutes or so at 350 degrees. Make sure the foil does't stick to the cheese before heating.
kind of adlibbed here, cut recipe in 1/2 added green chiles to bean mixture, used black and kidney beans. Sprayed with oil before baking then put in my airfryer for 5 minutes on 400. crispy good

These were addictive. I had to have two! My wife loved them also, and our picky two year old who only wants sugar filled food all the time enjoyed them. I took the advice of other reviewers and combined the sweet potato and red bean mash. That was easier and it tasted fantastic. I loaded them up with double the cheese and put olive oil on the outside of the tortillas before baking. The sweet potato I boiled, drained and mashed into the beans. I subsequently added no water to the mix. Served with guacamole, newman's own peach salsa, and sour cream spooned on top. yum! I have enough leftovers for the week too!!

I was skeptical of this recipe, thinking it would be bland, and was so pleasantly surprised at how it turned out! Only did a few things different than the original recipe: 2 tablespoons of chili powder instead of three, cooked the onion first, released the flavor of the garlic by cooking it for a minute with the onion, then added all the spices to the onion garlic mixture to release the flavor of the spices. I added all remaining ingredients to the warm pan to mix, but omitted the water as I didn’t want the same mashed consistency of the potatoes for the beans. I only roughly mashed the beans once added so there was more texture. We froze the remaining burritos for lunches/snacks as needed so we’ll see how that turns out too!! Will definitely be making these again. I’ll probably add green pepper next time too

These were very good and easy to make. I microwaved a big sweet potato cut in half with a little water in a glass dish for about 8 minutes turning once.The bean mixture came together quickly, I thought i added too much water but i just let it reduce a bit, which made all the spices fragrant. and used some grated almond pepper jack cheese. Instead of baking i used my panini press. I also used only one can of Simple Truth tribeans (black, pinto and kidney)and they were perfect for this recipe. It made 5 burritos in under 25 minutes.. not bad at all.

I made an easier version of this recipe for 4 people. After sauteing the onion and garlic I added about 1/3 cup of water and mixed in peeled, cubed sweet potatoes along with chickpeas (which are easier to digest). I used more potato than peas. While it was cooking I graded cheese. When it was done, about 20 min later, I added 1/3rd of the rest of the ingredients and mashed it all in the same pan. We spooned the mixture into tortillas. Served it with the cheese, sour cream and salsa. Excellent vegetarian meal and the cumin gives it a wonderful flavor. Thank you for sharing.

I took the advice of some of the people that made this after reading quite a few reviews. I used 1 can of kidney beans & 1 can of black beans as this is what I had in my pantry. I did not add any water to the beans. This would have made it too soupy. One reviewer added chopped cilantro to the bean mixture and I did this also. Good idea. I was surprised at how well the mustard & soy sauce enhanced the flavors. I will make this again.

I’ve made these for years now, only thing I change is I bake them instead of fry and use either leftover pinto beans or refried beans and top with salsa and cheese. This is probably my husbands favorite burritos. Oh and I have also used squash in place of the sweet potatoes.
I made several changes as most people have suggested. Added corn and used broth instead of water. I was pleasantly surprised by how good these were. Would def make again.
Made it for a friend gathering and it was a hit! Super tasty. Didn’t have 4 cans of beans, subbed with 2 cans black beans, 1 can pinto and a handful of frozen corn. Yum!
Wonderful substitutions on a winter day ! Used gf tortillas. Didn’t fold like a burrito but still tasted great

This recipe has been in my rotation for years now. I used to make them as written and they were delicious, and now I make them without the onions and garlic and they are just as good. They reheat beautifully when frozen!

I would definitely make it again. I had a large can of kidney beans that needed to be used, which is how I found this recipe. I used what was on hand, so there were a few changes from the original recipe: -Subbed shredded mozzarella -Subbed paprika because no chili powder or cayenne pepper - Added corn - Eyeballed the water amount, and used enough to make sure the bean mash wasn't dry. I didn't rinse the beans before adding them to the pan, so there was liquid already available -Overstuffed tortillas, so used fewer -Served with salsa and sour cream Husband loved it.

Best Daniel Fast meal so far. I'm a total carnivore but still like bean burritos. I made this twice. A couple take aways 1.) As suggested by others, make half a batch. This makes alot of food. I ended up using 2 cans of kidney beans and 2 cups of pre-cooked red yams. 2.) Starting with sauted onions with seasonings and last minute garlic. Followed by 2 kidney beans with light mash. Followed by cubed cooked yams. Then mashed all together. 3.) Then spread on waiting tortilla with cheese and sour cream. Very Good!
Kind of bland. And two cups of water??? It's like trying to roll soup into a burrito. By the time I am able to doctor it up enough to make it good I might as well use a different recipe all together.
